title: Property & Casualty
meta_description: P&C economics live in two moments: pricing the risk before the event and handling the claim after it.

blocks.x: P&C economics live in two moments: pricing the risk before the event and handling the claim after it. Both are decision factories — rate against exposure and catastrophe models, settle against policy language and fraud signals — and both reward carriers whose document and data machinery is industrialized.

The workflows we industrialize here: FNOL and claims triage, Estimate review and leakage control, Commercial risk surveying, Pricing/filing analytics, Cat exposure management. Each arrives with its current cycle times measured in the Diagnose phase, and each leaves the program governed by outcome SLOs rather than anecdotes.

items: FNOL, estimates, medical and police files arrive as documents; triage takes days and leakage hides in the queue.
Telematics and GLM pricing outrun validation and filing capacity; model risk documentation is rebuilt under exam.
Commercial properties and fleets lack sensor feeds; perils (water, freeze, telematics) are priced blind and prevented worse.
Underwriting exposure and claims experience never meet; portfolio steering is retrospective.
Third-party handlers hold sensitive claims data with uneven controls; the carrier owns the headline risk.
Catastrophe model ensembles strain HPC; uncertainty quantification is truncated.

blocks.x: How we help — five priority capabilities

items: documents classified/extracted; straight-through for clean claims with audit replay — triage in minutes
repair estimates benchmarked against parts/labor data with anomaly flags — leakage down 15-25%
exposure + claims unified with lineage for actuaries — steering analytics real
water/freeze/telematics sensors feeding prevention and pricing — peril frequency down on covered sites
third-party tiers, access reviews and evidence automation — handler risk governed
